newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks rise at end of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks rise at end of weekly trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares tended higher at the end of weekly trade on Wednesday on strong portfolio demand and outside interest in leading industrials, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.55 percent to 154.17 points in trade worth 357,885 dinars ($505,487) dominated by a few large deals in attractively valued blue-chip.
Dealers said buying activity was mainly triggered by outside funds for a number of industrials including Jordan Phosphates and Jordan Cement which helped pull along local investors.
Sustained optimism after the government passed two key investment reform laws this week is also helping to underpin the bourse.

"There was demand from foreign buyers who were collecting large quantities of some stock... and local portfolio interest grows when foreigners buy," said Ibrahim Odeh, from Wataniyeh Financial Services.
The two busiest stock, Jordan Cement and Jordan Phosphates, both gained in heavy trade, rising 0.03 dinars to 3.75 dinars and 3.33 dinars respectively.
Another focus of foreign interest was Arab Potash which was unchanged at 6.10 dinars in trade worth 19,975 dinars.
Jordan-Kuwait Bank, focus of speculation about a revived merger plan with Bank of Jordan, rose by 0.01 dinars to 2.57 dinars in one of the busiest volumes of trade worth 32,550 dinars.
A two dinar rise in Arab Bank to 259.000 dinars also helped buttress the overall bourse, dealers said.
Overall rising stocks outnumbered fallers by 21 to 14, with another 12 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.30 percent to 79.77 points, still 4.35 percent down from the start of the year.
